1

Coordinates

Start with a 64-bit ruler

Graph Paper divides a ruler into 64 equal bits. Fields select usable space on that ruler, and layouts arrange content within it. Related sections can share alignment while choosing different proportions. Begin with the content’s reading order, then choose the spatial relationships that make its hierarchy clear.

Get started

2

Usable space

Choose a field

Full uses 64 bits, Neat 60, Thin 59, Wide 58, and Ruled 56. These choices control outer insets and horizontal gutters. They do not set typography or decide when the layout changes.

Compare fields

3

Responsive design

Let layout, allocation, traversal, gutters, padding, and vertical spacing carry forward independently

Choose layouts explicitly at the viewport widths that suit your content. A selection carries forward until another replaces it. A later layout can change the arrangement without resetting the other choices. Test the narrowest important region with its intended text and images rather than assuming that every proportion works at every width.

Plan responsive layouts

4

Reading sequence

Source order comes first

Visual placement does not rewrite the HTML. Reading order, keyboard order, and the stacked presentation follow the source. Check that the sequence remains meaningful when spatial emphasis changes.

Author a composition

5

Hierarchy

Change the balance

Proportions describe the physical widths of the regions. A wider region can give an item emphasis, but its image, headline, treatment, and amount of content still determine what readers notice.

Explore layout vocabulary

6

Occupancy

Allocation is separate from proportion

Automatic allocation distributes consecutive source runs among regions. Exact physical counts refine eligible compositions. Neither choice changes the source sequence. Keep a collection of repeated peers distinct from an editorial composition whose regions carry different amounts of material.

Understand allocation
